name: UK company financial screener
demand: The official register contained 5.48 million records at 31 March 2026 and was accessed 14.6 billion times in FY2025–26; Companies House also accepted 16.5 million filings that year. These show a large, frequently used data source, not unique users or paying screener customers: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/companies-house-annual-report-and-accounts-2025-to-2026/companies-house-annual-report-and-accounts-2025-to-2026. I found no verified keyword-search volume or paying-customer count.
prices: Current published asking prices: CompanyStack Pro £19/month and API Starter £29/month, with API Business at £99/month: https://companystack.co.uk/pricing?product=app. Endole lists £39/month or £25/month billed annually: https://www.endole.co.uk/pricing/. CompanyPulse lists Professional at £23.99/month billed annually and Business at £79.20/month billed annually: https://www.companypulse.co.uk/pricing. DataLedger's API plans start at £10/month, and its custom financial datasets start at £295: https://dataledger.uk/faqs and https://dataledger.uk/pricing. These are advertised prices, not evidence of completed sales.
copy_speed: CompanyStack is already a direct match: its free tier screens the first 25 results and Pro includes the full financial screener: https://companystack.co.uk/pricing?product=app. For the 23 Apr–23 Oct 2026 window, I found no verified launch date for a new UK-only clone. Dated competitive releases do show rapid copying: Registrum shipped a hosted, keyless UK-company MCP endpoint on 7 Aug 2026, after its API and account parsing launched in February: https://www.registrum.co.uk/articles/what-we-shipped. CompanyPulse added a £99/month Business tier on 12 Jul 2026; the platform itself launched earlier: https://www.companypulse.co.uk/changelog. Global Database made its Regis company-intelligence agent generally available on 30 Jun 2026 and its API on 24 Jul; this is a broad, global competitor rather than a UK-only screener: https://www.globaldatabase.com/regis-is-now-live-the-agentic-ai-for-official-registry-data-is-open-to-everyone and https://www.globaldatabase.com/global-database-launches-its-company-verification-ai---regis. DataLedger's service terms are effective 7 Apr 2026, but that does not verify its launch date: https://dataledger.uk/terms.
platform_risk: Companies House exposes a live API and free bulk company and accounts data products, so competitors can obtain the underlying register without buying this product: https://developer.company-information.service.gov.uk/ and https://www.gov.uk/guidance/companies-house-data-products. The value is in parsing, matching and maintaining the data; the service depends on Companies House filings and formats. Companies House says its accounts data products contain XBRL/iXBRL files rather than ready-made screening figures: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/companies-house-data-products. CompanyStack also says its figures are taken from filings, are not audited, and its health score is not a credit rating: https://companystack.co.uk/ and https://companystack.co.uk/docs.
defensible_asset: There is a compiled-data asset, but it is not exclusive. CompanyStack reports 24.8 million parsed account-years across 3.6 million active companies and 16 million owner/controller records, counted 4 Oct 2026: https://companystack.co.uk/. Maintaining account parsing, ownership links and source dates takes sustained work. However, Endole advertises 10-year financial trends, Registrum documents iXBRL and PDF parsing, and DataLedger sells structured financial and ownership data: https://www.endole.co.uk/pricing/, https://www.registrum.co.uk/articles/what-we-shipped and https://dataledger.uk/pricing. API integrations and monitoring could create switching costs after adoption, but the data moat is moderate at best and there is no evident network effect.
build_effort: High, with substantial ongoing data-quality work: ingest and refresh Companies House records; parse iXBRL and less-structured accounts; normalize sparse financial histories; connect PSC ownership; expose screening, exports, alerts and an API; and keep source provenance visible. CompanyStack describes daily sync and software parsing with OCR for PDF or paper filings, while Registrum documents its separate parsing and ownership work: https://companystack.co.uk/ and https://www.registrum.co.uk/articles/what-we-shipped. This is an estimate based on the product scope, not a verified build timeline.
channel: Inbound only: SEO pages with dated sample results, API or MCP directories, integrations and self-serve sign-up; no cold email, SMS, DM or calls. Contextual search ads are another option, but UK online-ad tracking and storage technologies require consent; ICO guidance says contextual advertising is more readily compatible with PECR and UK GDPR than behavioral targeting: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/how-do-the-rules-apply-to-online-advertising/. Check local rules before running ads in each other target country.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified: no operating history or owner-time evidence. The ≤5-hour limit cannot be supported from public sources; expect heavier founder involvement during build, launch and data incidents.
automation_reason: Estimate: scheduled ingestion, routine parsing, screening, exports, alerts, billing and first-line documentation support can be automated. Human review remains important for parser regressions, ambiguous filings, security incidents and decisions about how to describe risk. CompanyStack documents automated data refresh and a rules-based score with no analyst adjustment, which supports automation potential but does not verify this proposed business's actual share: https://companystack.co.uk/ and https://companystack.co.uk/docs.
moat_assessment: Passes the compiled-data moat requirement in form, but the moat is weak for a generic build: the source records are public and free to obtain, and several vendors already sell normalized financial histories, ownership links, screening or monitoring. CompanyStack's own free and paid tiers already cover the proposed core product: https://companystack.co.uk/pricing?product=app. Build only with a sharper buyer workflow or genuinely harder-to-replicate data and quality advantage; ordinary company search plus financial ratios is readily copied.
desk_test: Within one workday, hand-build a sample screen for one specific buyer workflow from public filings, show sourced sample results on a one-page site, and offer a clearly described self-serve paid pilot at the existing £29/month CompanyStack API Starter price point: https://companystack.co.uk/pricing?product=app. Publish through SEO or an API directory and use contextual search ads only with appropriate consent. Treat a paid pilot as the pass signal; a waitlist signup alone does not prove willingness to pay.
red_flags: No verified revenue, churn, or paying-customer evidence was found; published competitor prices are not transaction proof. CompanyStack is already the exact competitor and offers the full screener for £19/month, with a limited free screener: https://companystack.co.uk/pricing?product=app. Its site says only 2.0% of active companies' latest accounts showed turnover as of 4 Oct 2026, limiting revenue-based screening coverage: https://companystack.co.uk/. Its API docs say the health score has not been statistically tested against company failures: https://companystack.co.uk/docs. A generic clone therefore faces low price ceilings, sparse P&L data and a weakly differentiated data moat.
